html:
The Rose Revolution was a peaceful change of power in Georgia in November 2003, when protests over rigged elections forced President Eduard Shevardnadze to resign.

On 22 November protesters led by Mikheil Saakashvili burst into parliament carrying roses as Shevardnadze spoke, and he resigned the next day. Saakashvili was elected president in January 2004. His government fired the corrupt traffic police, cut red tape and crime, and pushed for membership of NATO and the European Union, which angered Russia. Critics later accused him of abusing power. The revolution inspired the Orange Revolution in Ukraine a year later, and its tensions with Moscow led to the war of 2008.
sum: The Rose Revolution was a peaceful change of power in Georgia in November 2003, when protests over rigged elections forced President Eduard Shevardnadze to resign.
